title: Nonzero polynomial formal fibres in characteristic zero
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian complete local domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] with fraction field [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] of characteristic zero, $q$ a maximal ideal of $A[x]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] contracting to the maximal ideal of $A$, and $0\ne r\subseteq q$ a prime contracting to zero in $A$. Then $\kappa(r)\otimes_{A[x]}(A[x]_q)^\wedge$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] is geometrically regular over $\kappa(r)$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring].

source.place: Proof of Proposition 07PV, paragraphs 3--4, nonzero characteristic-zero case; derivation repair from the second paragraph of the proof of Lemma 07PU, using 07PE and 07PF.

proof.text:
1. By 032D choose a regular complete local subring A₀ with A finite over A₀.
   Contract q and r to q₀ and r₀. Finiteness makes the polynomial map quasi-finite
   at q, q₀ maximal, and r₀ a prime above zero. By 07PP(1) it suffices to treat A₀.

2. The fraction field K₀ of A₀ has characteristic zero by its embedding in that
   of A. The completion C₀ of A₀[X] at q₀ is regular by polynomial smoothness,
   smooth ascent (07NF), regular local localization, and completion regularity (07NY).
   If r₀ is zero, the fibre is a localization of C₀, hence regular.

3. Otherwise r₀K₀[X] is a nonzero prime of the PID K₀[X], generated by an
   irreducible polynomial f. Localizing C₀ at the nonzero elements of A₀ gives
   a regular ring R, and the formal fibre is R/fR. This follows by localizing
   the quotient A₀[X]/r₀, whose fraction field is K₀[X]/(f).

4. The derivation d/dX extends through localization, completion, and localization
   at A₀ minus zero (07PE), and sends f to f'. In characteristic zero, irreducibility
   gives gcd(f,f') = 1. A Bezout identity therefore makes D(f) a unit modulo f.
   The hypersurface derivation criterion (07PF) makes R/fR regular.

5. The residue field at r₀ has characteristic zero, so every finite purely
   inseparable extension is trivial. Noetherianity follows from completion and
   localization/quotient. Thus the fibre is geometrically regular. Apply 07PP(1)
   to conclude for A.

lean.statement:
theorem completeLocalNonzeroFibreCharZero
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A]
    (q : Ideal (Polynomial A)) [q.IsMaximal]
    (hq : q.comap (Polynomial.C : A →+* Polynomial A) = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A)
    [CharZero (Localization.AtPrime (⊥ : Ideal A))]
    (r : Ideal (Polynomial A)) [r.IsPrime] (hrq : r ≤ q) (hr : r ≠ ⊥)
    (hrA : r.comap (Polynomial.C : A →+* Polynomial A) = ⊥) :
    Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular r.ResidueField
      (r.Fiber (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q))
        (Localization.AtPrime q)))
